\]

For a prime number \(p\) with \(p\nmid 30\) let \(X_{p}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{Z}}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb{F}_{p}\) be the reduction of \(X\) modulo \(p\), and denote  

\[
N(p)=\# X_{p}(\mathbb{F}_{p}).
\]

The variety \(X_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}\) is a smooth, geometrically irreducible plane curve of degree \(30\).  
Using the Lang–Weil estimate for a geometrically irreducible projective variety of dimension \(d\) and degree \(\delta\),

\[
\#X_{p}(\mathbb{F}_{p})=\delta\,p^{d}+O\!\left(p^{d-\frac12}\right),
\]

determine the limit  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{N(p)}{p}.
\]

Put your final answer inside \boxed{}.

The curve \(X\) is a smooth, geometrically irreducible projective variety of dimension  

\[
d=\dim X = 1 ,
\]

and it is a hypersurface of degree  

\[
\delta = 30 .
\]

\[
N(p)=\#X_{p}(\mathbf{F}_{p}) = \delta \, p^{d}+ O\!\bigl(p^{d-\frac12}\bigr)
      = 30\,p + O\!\bigl(p^{1/2}\bigr).
\]

Dividing by \(p\) and letting \(p\to\infty\),

\[
\frac{N(p)}{p}=30 + O\!\bigl(p^{-1/2}\bigr)\longrightarrow 30 .
\]

Hence  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{N(p)}{p}=30 .
\]

\[
\boxed{30}
\]

\[
\#X_{p}(\mathbf F_{p}) = \delta\, p^{d}+O\!\bigl(p^{d-\frac12}\bigr).

\[
N(p)=\#X_{p}(\mathbf F_{p}) = 30\,p + O\!\bigl(p^{1/2}\bigr).

\[

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{N(p)}{p}=1 .

\boxed{1.0000}

The Lang–Weil estimate for a geometrically irreducible projective variety of

\[

problems.skill: Lang–Weil point‑count estimate for varieties over finite fields
problems.problem:
Let \(X\subset \mathbf{P}^{4}_{\mathbb{Z}}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbb{Z}[X_{0},\dots ,X_{4}]\) be a smooth geometrically irreducible three‑dimensional projective variety.  
Let \(Y\subset \mathbf{P}^{5}_{\mathbb{Z}}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbb{Z}[Y_{0},\dots ,Y_{5}]\) be another smooth geometrically irreducible three‑dimensional projective variety and let  

\[
\pi : Y\longrightarrow X
\]

be the morphism obtained by restricting the linear projection
\([Y_{0}:\dots :Y_{5}]\mapsto [Y_{0}:\dots :Y_{4}]\).  
Assume that \(\pi\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\) over \(\mathbb{Z}\).  
Let \(V\subset X\) be the dense open subscheme over which \(\pi\) is finite étale (so \(\pi^{-1}(V)\to V\) is a finite étale cover of degree \(31\)).  

For each prime \(p\) denote by \(V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) the set of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points of \(V\) and define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x).
\]

Using the Lang–Weil estimate, compute \(\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor\). Put your final answer inside \boxed{}.
all_solutions:
The morphism \(\pi : Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant geometric degree \(31\).  
For a prime \(p\) let  

\[
N_X(p)=\#V(\mathbf F_p),\qquad N_Y(p)=\#\pi^{-1}(V)(\mathbf F_p)
\]

(the latter equals the number of \(\mathbf F_p\)-points of \(Y\) that lie over \(V\)).  
Because \(\pi\) is étale over \(V\),

\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=N_Y(p).
\]

Hence  

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\frac{N_Y(p)}{N_X(p)} .
\]

Both \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth projective three‑folds, so by the Lang–Weil estimate  

\[
\#X(\mathbf F_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),\qquad 
\#Y(\mathbf F_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),
\]

the same main term \(p^{3}\) appears for any smooth projective variety of dimension \(3\).  
Consequently  

\[
\frac{N_Y(p)}{N_X(p)}=1+O\!\left(p^{-1/2}\right)\xrightarrow[p\to\infty]{}1 .
\]

Therefore  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=1 .
\]

Finally  

\[
\Big\lfloor 100L\Big\rfloor=\big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor = 100 .
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The morphism \(\pi : Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\) over the open set \(V\subset X\).  
For a prime \(p\),

\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\#\bigl(Y(\mathbf F_p)\cap\pi^{-1}(V)\bigr)
\]

i.e. the number of \(\mathbf F_p\)-points of \(Y\) lying over \(V\).

Both \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth, geometrically irreducible three‑dimensional varieties.  
By the Lang–Weil estimate, for large \(p\)

\[
\#V(\mathbf F_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),\qquad 
\#Y(\mathbf F_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}).
\]

The complement \(X\setminus V\) (and likewise \(\pi^{-1}(X\setminus V)\)) has codimension \(\ge 1\); its \(\mathbf F_p\)-points are \(O(p^{2})\). Hence

\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)
= \#Y(\mathbf F_p) + O(p^{2})
= p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}).
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)
= \frac{p^{3}+O(p^{5/2})}{p^{3}+O(p^{5/2})}\longrightarrow 1
\qquad(p\to\infty).
\]

Thus \(L = 1\). Consequently

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The morphism \(\pi : Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\).  
For a point \(x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(x)\) is a finite étale \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-scheme of degree \(31\); its \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-points are precisely the points of the fibre that are fixed by the Frobenius automorphism.  

Summing over all \(x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\),

\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\#\pi^{-1}\bigl(V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\bigr)
= \#Y(\mathbf{F}_{p})+O(p^{2}),
\]

because the complement of \(V\) in \(X\) (and its pre‑image in \(Y\)) has dimension \(\le 2\), giving only \(O(p^{2})\) points.

Both \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth, geometrically irreducible three‑dimensional projective varieties.  
By the Lang–Weil estimate,

\[
\#X(\mathbf{F}_{p}) = p^{3}+O(p^{2}),\qquad 
\#Y(\mathbf{F}_{p}) = p^{3}+O(p^{2}).
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)
= \frac{\#Y(\mathbf{F}_{p})+O(p^{2})}{\#X(\mathbf{F}_{p})+O(p^{2})}
= \frac{p^{3}+O(p^{2})}{p^{3}+O(p^{2})}\longrightarrow 1
\quad (p\to\infty).
\]

Therefore  

\[
L = \lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=1.
\]

Finally  

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The morphism \(\pi : Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\) over \(\mathbb Z\).  
For a point \(x\in V(\mathbf F_p)\) the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(x)\) is a finite étale \(\mathbf F_p\)-scheme of degree \(31\).  
Geometrically the fibre consists of \(31\) points permuted by the Frobenius element
\(\operatorname{Frob}_p\) inside the Galois group \(G\) of the covering.  
The number of \(\mathbf F_p\)-rational points in the fibre equals the number of fixed
points of this permutation.

Because the covering is transitive, the action of \(G\) on the \(31\) geometric
points is transitive.  For any transitive action the average number of fixed
points of an element of \(G\) is

\[
\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(g)=\frac{|{\text{orbits}}|}{1}=1 .
\]

By the Chebotarev density theorem (or the Lang–Weil estimate) the Frobenius
elements become equidistributed in \(G\) as \(p\to\infty\).  Hence

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=1 .
\]

Therefore  

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor =\big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor =100 .
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The morphism \(\pi:Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\).  
For any finite field \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\),

\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\#\pi^{-1}\bigl(V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\bigr)=\#Y(\mathbb{F}_{p}),
\]

because each \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-point of \(Y\) lies over exactly one \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-point of \(X\).

Hence

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=
\frac{\#Y(\mathbb{F}_{p})}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}.
\]

Both \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth, geometrically irreducible three‑dimensional projective varieties.  
By the Lang–Weil estimate,

\[
\#X(\mathbb{F}_{p}) = p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),\qquad 
\#Y(\mathbb{F}_{p}) = p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}).
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac{\#Y(\mathbb{F}_{p})}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\longrightarrow 1\qquad(p\to\infty),
\]

so

\[
L = 1.
\]

Finally,

\[
\big\lfloor 100L \big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100 \times 1 \big\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The sum in the numerator is just the number of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-points of the pre‑image of the open set \(V\):
\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\#\bigl(\pi^{-1}(V)\bigr)(\mathbb{F}_p).
\]

Because \(\pi\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\), the scheme \(\pi^{-1}(V)\) is a smooth, geometrically irreducible three‑dimensional variety over \(\mathbb{Z}\) (it is a dense open of the smooth three‑fold \(Y\)).

For any smooth geometrically irreducible \(d\)-dimensional variety \(Z\) over \(\mathbb{Z}\), the Lang–Weil estimate gives
\[
\#Z(\mathbb{F}_p)=p^{d}+O\!\left(p^{d-\frac12}\right)\qquad (p\to\infty).
\]

Applying this to both \(V\) and \(\pi^{-1}(V)\) (each of dimension \(3\)) we obtain
\[
\#V(\mathbb{F}_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),\qquad
\#\bigl(\pi^{-1}(V)\bigr)(\mathbb{F}_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}).
\]

Hence
\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_p)}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(x)
= \frac{\#\bigl(\pi^{-1}(V)\bigr)(\mathbb{F}_p)}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_p)}
\longrightarrow 1 \quad\text{as } p\to\infty .
\]

Therefore \(L=1\) and
\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor=\big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor = 100 .
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

For the morphism  

\[
\pi : Y\longrightarrow X
\]

the hypothesis says that \(\pi\) is **finite étale of constant degree \(31\) over \(\mathbb Z\)**.  
Hence for every field \(k\) (in particular for each finite field \(\mathbf F_{p}\)) the base‑change  

\[
\pi_{k}:Y_{k}\longrightarrow X_{k}
\]

is a finite étale map of degree \(31\).

---

### Counting points over \(\mathbf F_{p}\)

Both \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth projective three‑folds, so by the Lang–Weil estimate  

\[
\#X(\mathbf F_{p}) = p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),\qquad 
\#Y(\mathbf F_{p}) = p^{3}+O(p^{5/2}),
\]

and the same estimate holds for any dense open subscheme such as \(V\subset X\).

Because \(\pi\) is finite étale of degree \(31\),

\[
\#Y(\mathbf F_{p}) = 31\;\#X(\mathbf F_{p})+O(p^{5/2}).
\]

The complement \(X\setminus V\) has codimension \(\ge 1\); its \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-points are \(O(p^{2})\), which is negligible compared with \(p^{3}\). Therefore

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(V(\mathbf F_{p})) = 31\;\#V(\mathbf F_{p})+O(p^{5/2}).
\]

Dividing by \(\#V(\mathbf F_{p})\) we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)

      = 31 + O(p^{-1/2}),
\]

and the error term tends to \(0\) as \(p\to\infty\).

Hence the limit defined in the problem exists and equals the degree of the cover:

\[
L = \lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=31.
\]

---

### Final computation

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100\times 31\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 3100\big\rfloor = 3100.
\]

\[
\boxed{3100}
\]

The sum of the fibre sizes over the \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-points of \(V\) equals the number of \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-points of \(Y\) (up to a negligible error coming from the complement of \(V\)).

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)

Both \(X\) and \(Y\) are smooth projective three‑folds, so by the Lang–Weil estimate

and \(\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p}) = \#X(\mathbf{F}_{p})+O(p^{2})\).

\[
\frac{\#Y(\mathbf{F}_{p})}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}=1+O(p^{-1})\xrightarrow[p\to\infty]{}1.

\[

\[
\big\lfloor 100L \big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100 \times 1 \big\rfloor = 100.
\]

\boxed{100}
\]

The morphism \(\pi : Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\) over the dense open subset \(V\subset X\).

\[

\]

the number of \(\mathbb F_p\)-points of the open three‑fold \(\pi^{-1}(V)\subset Y\).

=\frac{\#\pi^{-1}(V)(\mathbb F_p)}{\#V(\mathbb F_p)}
\longrightarrow \frac{31\,p^{3}}{p^{3}}=31 \qquad (p\to\infty).
\]

Therefore  

\[
L = 31.
\]

Finally,

\[
\big\lfloor 100L \big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100 \times 31 \big\rfloor = \boxed{3100}.

For the smooth three–dimensional projective varieties \(X\) and \(Y\) we have, by the Lang–Weil estimate,

\[
\#X(\mathbf F_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{2}), \qquad 
\#Y(\mathbf F_p)=p^{3}+O(p^{2}) .

The morphism \(\pi:Y\to X\) is finite étale of constant degree \(31\); the set where it fails to be étale is a proper closed subset of \(X\) of codimension \(\ge 1\). Hence

\[
\#V(\mathbf F_p)=\#X(\mathbf F_p)+O(p^{2})=p^{3}+O(p^{2}).

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}
\frac{\#Y(\mathbf F_p)+O(p^{2})}{\#X(\mathbf F_p)+O(p^{2})}
=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{p^{3}+O(p^{2})}{p^{3}+O(p^{2})}=1 .
\]

\[
\Big\lfloor 100L\Big\rfloor=\big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor = 100 .

V(\mathbb{F}_{p})=\bigl\{\,y\in Y(\mathbb{F}_{p}) \mid \text{the fibre }\pi^{-1}(y)

The morphism  

\[
\pi:X\longrightarrow Y,\qquad 
X=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1},x]/(x^{6}-(t^{3}+2))\Bigr),\;
Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]
\]

is finite of degree \(6\).  
For a prime \(p\) and a point \(y\in Y(\mathbb F_{p})\) we have \(y\leftrightarrow a\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) (the value of the coordinate \(t\)).  
The fibre over \(a\) is  

\[
\pi^{-1}(a)=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb F_{p}[x]/(x^{6}-(a^{3}+2))\bigr).
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  When is the fibre étale?

The fibre is étale over \(\mathbb F_{p}\) iff the polynomial  

\[
f_a(x)=x^{6}-(a^{3}+2)
\]

is separable.  
For \(p\neq 2,3\) we have \(f_a'(x)=6x^{5}\); the only possible repeated root is
\(x=0\).  This occurs exactly when \(a^{3}+2\equiv0\pmod p\).  
Hence for all sufficiently large primes  

\[
V(\mathbb F_{p})=\{a\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\mid a^{3}+2\neq0\}.
\]

(The finitely many primes \(p=2,3\) do not affect the limit.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Number of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points in a fibre

For \(a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) the \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points of the fibre are the
solutions of  

\[
x^{6}=c,\qquad c=a^{3}+2\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}.
\]

Let  

\[
d_p=\gcd(6,p-1).
\]

The map \(x\mapsto x^{6}\) on \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) has kernel of size \(d_p\)
and image of size \((p-1)/d_p\).  
Consequently

* if \(c\) lies in the image, there are exactly \(d_p\) solutions;
* otherwise there are none.

Because \(a\mapsto c=a^{3}+2\) is a polynomial of degree \(3\), as \(a\) varies
over \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) the values \(c\) are uniformly distributed in
\(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) (up to an error \(O(p^{-1})\)).  
Hence

\[
\Pr\bigl(c\text{ is a }6\text{‑th power}\bigr)=\frac{|{\rm Im}(x\mapsto x^{6})|}{p-1}
      =\frac{1}{d_p}.
\]

Therefore the expected number of solutions is  

\[
\mathbb E\bigl[\#\pi^{-1}(a)\bigr]
      = d_p\cdot\frac{1}{d_p}=1 .
\]

The same expectation holds for every residue class of \(p\) (including the
cases \(d_p=1,2,3,6\)).  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Averaging over the étale points

For each large prime \(p\),

\[
\#V(\mathbb F_{p}) = (p-1)-\#\{a\mid a^{3}=-2\}=p-2+O(1),
\]

so the set \(V(\mathbb F_{p})\) is asymptotically the whole \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\).
Since the expected fibre size over any \(a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) is \(1\),

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)
      = 1+o(1)\qquad (p\to\infty).
\]

Thus  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}
          \sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

\[

* the fibre is not étale only when the right–hand side is \(0\), i.e. when  
  \(a^{3}+2=0\).

Hence  

\[
V(\mathbb F_{p})=\Bigl\{a\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\mid a^{3}\neq-2\Bigr\},
\qquad 
\#V(\mathbb F_{p})=p-1-N_{p},
\]

where \(N_{p}\) is the number of solutions of \(a^{3}=-2\) in \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\).
For every \(p>3\) one has \(N_{p}=1\) on average, so asymptotically  

\[
\#V(\mathbb F_{p})\sim p .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Size of a geometric fibre

Let \(c=a^{3}+2\neq0\).  
In the cyclic group \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) of order \(p-1\),

\[
\#\{x\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid x^{6}=c\}= 
\begin{cases}
\gcd(6,p-1) & \text{if }c\text{ is a }6\text{‑th power},\\[2pt]
0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Denote \(d(p)=\gcd(6,p-1)\).  
For odd primes \(p\),

\[
d(p)=
\begin{cases}
6 & p\equiv 1\pmod 6,\\
2 & p\equiv 5\pmod 6 .
\end{cases}
\]

The image of the map \(x\mapsto x^{6}\) is a subgroup of index \(d(p)\); therefore
the proportion of elements of \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) that are \(6\)‑th powers is \(1/d(p)\).

Assuming the values \(c=a^{3}+2\) are uniformly distributed in \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\)
(the error is \(o(p)\)), we obtain

\[
\Pr\bigl(\#\pi^{-1}(a)=d(p)\bigr)=\frac{1}{d(p)},\qquad
\Pr\bigl(\#\pi^{-1}(a)=0\bigr)=1-\frac{1}{d(p)} .
\]

Consequently the **expected** size of the fibre over a point of \(V(\mathbb F_{p})\) is  

\[
\mathbf E\bigl[\#\pi^{-1}(a)\bigr]=
\frac{1}{d(p)}\cdot d(p)=1 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  The limit \(L\)

Hence for every large prime \(p\),

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(a)
\;=\;1+o(1),
\]

and the limit exists:

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(a)=1 .

Thus the geometric fibre consists of six points, and the Galois group of the covering
\(X\to Y\) is the group that permutes these six roots.

---

### Galois group

Over the function field \(\mathbb{Q}(t)\) the polynomial \(x^{6}-(t^{3}+2)\) is
irreducible and its splitting field is obtained by adjoining a primitive
6‑th root of unity \(\zeta_{6}\) and a chosen sixth root \(\alpha\) of \(t^{3}+2\).
Hence the Galois group is  

\[
G\simeq C_{6}\rtimes C_{2}\cong D_{6},
\]

the dihedral group of order \(12\).  
\(G\) acts transitively on the set \(S\) of six geometric points of a fibre.

---

### Number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points in a fibre

For a point \(y\) where the fibre is étale (i.e. \(p\) does not divide the
discriminant), the Frobenius element \(\mathrm{Frob}_{y}\in G\) is well defined.
The \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-rational points of the fibre are exactly the points of \(S\)
fixed by \(\mathrm{Frob}_{y}\).  
Thus  

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(y)=\#\operatorname{Fix}(\mathrm{Frob}_{y}).
\]

### Averaging via Chebotarev

Chebotarev’s density theorem tells us that, when \(p\) varies, the Frobenius
conjugacy classes become equidistributed in \(G\) (the set of ramified primes has
density 0, so they do not affect the limit). Consequently,

\[
\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}
\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)
= \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(g).
\]

For a transitive action of a finite group on a finite set, Burnside’s lemma gives  

\[
\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(g)=1 .
\]

Indeed, for \(G=D_{6}\) acting on the six vertices of a regular hexagon we have  

\[
\sum_{g\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(g)=6\;(\text{identity})+3\cdot2\;(\text{reflections through vertices})=12=|G|.
\]

Hence  

\[
L = 1 .

\end{cases}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Probability that \(c\) is a 6‑th power

The map \(a\mapsto a^{3}\) sends \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\) onto the subgroup of
cubes, which has index \(\gcd(3,n)\). Adding the constant \(2\) makes the
distribution of \(c=a^{3}+2\) essentially uniform on \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\);
the error is \(O(1/p)\) and disappears in the limit.

Hence, for a fixed prime \(p\),

\[
\Pr\bigl(c\in\operatorname{Im}\varphi\bigr)=\frac{\#\operatorname{Im}\varphi}{p-1}
      =\frac{(p-1)/d}{p-1}= \frac{1}{d}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Expected fibre size for a given \(p\)

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{a\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(a)
   = d\cdot\frac{1}{d}=1\qquad(\text{up to }O(1/p)).
\]

Thus the average equals \(1\) for each residue class of \(p\) modulo \(6\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 5.  Limit using Chebotarev

The cover \(X\to Y\) is a connected finite étale cover of degree \(6\)
over the generic fibre (\(p\neq2,3\)).  
For a transitive action of the Galois group on the six geometric points,
Chebotarev (or Burnside’s lemma) tells us that the average number of
\(\mathbf F_{p}\)-rational points in a fibre is exactly \(1\).

Therefore  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}
        \sum_{y\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 6.  Requested quantity

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor =\big\lfloor 100\cdot1\big\rfloor =100.
\]

\boxed{100}

The morphism  

\[
\pi:X\longrightarrow Y,\qquad 
Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t,t^{-1}],\qquad 
X=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbf Z[t,t^{-1},x]/(x^{6}-(t^{3}+2))\Bigr)
\]

is given fibrewise, for a prime \(p\) and a point \(y\) corresponding to a
\(t\in\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast}\), by  

\[
\pi^{-1}(y)=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbf F_{p}[x]/(x^{6}-(t^{3}+2))\bigr).
\]

Hence  

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(y)=\#\{x\in\mathbf F_{p}\mid x^{6}=t^{3}+2\}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Étale points  

The fibre is étale over \(\mathbf F_{p}\) iff the polynomial
\(x^{6}-(t^{3}+2)\) is separable, i.e. iff  

* \(p\neq 2,3\) (otherwise the derivative \(6x^{5}\) vanishes), and  
* \(t^{3}+2\neq0\) (otherwise the root \(x=0\) would be multiple).

Thus for all sufficiently large primes  

\[
V(\mathbf F_{p})=\{\,t\in\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast}\mid t^{3}+2\neq0\,\},
\qquad 
\#V(\mathbf F_{p})=p-1-O(1).
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Number of solutions of \(x^{6}=a\)

Let \(a=t^{3}+2\neq0\).  
In the cyclic group \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast}\) (order \(p-1\)) the map  

\[
\phi:\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast}\longrightarrow\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast},\qquad
\phi(x)=x^{6}
\]

has kernel of size  

\[
d:=\gcd(6,p-1),
\]

and image of size \((p-1)/d\).  
Consequently

\[
\#\{x\in\mathbf F_{p}\mid x^{6}=a\}= 
\begin{cases}
d &\text{if }a\in\operatorname{Im}\phi\;(=\text{6‑th powers}),\\[2mm]
0 &\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Probability that \(t^{3}+2\) is a 6‑th power  

For a fixed prime \(p\) the values \(t^{3}+2\) with \(t\in\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast}\)
are uniformly distributed over \(\mathbf F_{p}\) (up to an error \(O(p^{-1/2})\)
by Weil bounds).  
Hence, disregarding the negligible case \(t^{3}+2=0\),

\[
\Pr\bigl(t^{3}+2\text{ is a 6‑th power}\bigr)=\frac{1}{d}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Average size of the fibre for a given \(p\)

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)
   =\frac{1}{p-1+O(1)}\sum_{t\in\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast}\,;\,t^{3}+2\neq0}
      \bigl[d\cdot\mathbf 1_{\{t^{3}+2\in (\mathbf F_{p}^{\ast})^{6}\}}\bigr].
\]

Using the probability computed above, the average tends to  

\[
d\cdot\frac{1}{d}=1\qquad (p\to\infty).
\]

Thus the limit defined in the problem exists and equals  

\[
L=1.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

\[
\big\lfloor100L\big\rfloor=\big\lfloor100\cdot1\big\rfloor=100.
\]

The morphism  

\[
\pi : X\longrightarrow Y ,\qquad 
X=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb Z[t,x]/(x^{4}-(t^{2}+5))\bigr),\; 
Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t]
\]

is finite of degree 4.  
It is étale exactly where the discriminant of the polynomial  
\(x^{4}-(t^{2}+5)\) does not vanish.  
The discriminant is  

\[
\Delta =256\,(t^{2}+5)^{3},
\]

so the étale locus is  

\[
V = Y \setminus\bigl\{2\}\cup\{t\mid t^{2}+5=0\}.
\]

For a prime \(p\neq 2\) we have  

\[
V(\mathbb F_{p})=\{\,t\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid t^{2}+5\neq0\,\}.
\]

For such a \(t\) put \(a=t^{2}+5\neq0\).  
The fibre \(\pi^{-1}(t)\) is the set of solutions of  

\[
x^{4}=a\qquad\text{in }\mathbb F_{p}.
\]

---

### Number of solutions of \(x^{4}=a\)

*If \(p\equiv1\pmod 4\):*  
\(|\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}|=p-1\) is divisible by 4.  
The map \(x\mapsto x^{4}\) has kernel of size 4, and its image is the subgroup of fourth powers, which has index 4.  
Hence  

\[
\#\{x\mid x^{4}=a\}=
\begin{cases}
4 &\text{if }a\in(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times})^{4},\\[2pt]
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

*If \(p\equiv3\pmod 4\):*  
\(\gcd(4,p-1)=2\).  
Now the image of \(x\mapsto x^{4}\) equals the set of quadratic residues, and each quadratic residue has exactly 2 pre‑images. Thus  

\[
\#\{x\mid x^{4}=a\}=
\begin{cases}
2 &\text{if }a\text{ is a square},\\[2pt]
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

---

### Average number of points in a fibre

For a fixed prime \(p\neq2\) let  

\[
S(p)=\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t).
\]

Because the map \(t\mapsto a=t^{2}+5\) is a non‑constant quadratic polynomial, the values \(a\) are (up to the negligible set where \(a=0\)) uniformly distributed in \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\).  
Consequently:

* when \(p\equiv1\pmod4\) the probability that a random non‑zero \(a\) is a fourth power is \(1/4\);
* when \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) the probability that a random non‑zero \(a\) is a square is \(1/2\).

Therefore  

\[
\frac{S(p)}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}
=
\begin{cases}
4\cdot\frac14 = 1 & (p\equiv1\!\!\pmod4),\\[4pt]
2\cdot\frac12 = 1 & (p\equiv3\!\!\pmod4).
\end{cases}
\]

The two cases give the same value, and the finitely many excluded primes (notably \(p=2\)) do not affect the limit. Hence

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1.
\]

\[
\Delta = (2)\cup (t^{2}+5)\subset \operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t].

\[
V(\mathbf F_p)=\{\,t\in\mathbf F_p\mid t^{2}+5\neq0\,\},
\qquad 
\#V(\mathbf F_p)=p-N_p,
\]

For \(t\in V(\mathbf F_p)\) the fibre is  

\[
\pi^{-1}(t)=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbf F_p[x]/(x^{4}-(t^{2}+5))\bigr),
\]

\[
x^{4}=a,\qquad a:=t^{2}+5\neq0,
\]

---

### 1.  Number of solutions of \(x^{4}=a\)

Let \(d=\gcd(4,p-1)\).  
The kernel of the map \(x\mapsto x^{4}\) on \(\mathbf F_p^{\!*}\) has size \(d\); therefore

\[
\#\{x\in\mathbf F_p\mid x^{4}=a\}= 
\begin{cases}
d & \text{if } a\in (\mathbf F_p^{\!*})^{4},\\[2pt]
0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus  

* if \(p\equiv1\pmod4\): \(d=4\) and we need \(a\) to be a **fourth power**;  
* if \(p\equiv3\pmod4\): \(d=2\) and a fourth power coincides with a **square**, so we only need \(a\) to be a square.

---

### 2.  Proportion of \(t\) for which \(a\) is a square

Let \(\chi\) be the Legendre symbol. For \(a\neq0\),

\[
\mathbf 1_{\text{square}}(a)=\frac{1+\chi(a)}{2}.
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{1}{p}\sum_{t\in\mathbf F_p}\mathbf 1_{\text{square}}(t^{2}+5)
      =\frac12+\frac{1}{2p}\sum_{t\in\mathbf F_p}\chi(t^{2}+5).
\]

The quadratic polynomial \(t^{2}+5\) has discriminant \(-20\neq0\) for all
\(p>5\); a classical result gives  

\[
\sum_{t\in\mathbf F_p}\chi(t^{2}+5)=-\chi(1)=-1 .
\]

Consequently  

\[
\frac{1}{p}\#\{t\mid t^{2}+5\text{ is a square}\}= \frac12-\frac1{2p}
\longrightarrow \frac12 .
\]

Thus for \(p\equiv3\pmod4\)

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(t)
   =2\cdot\frac12+o(1)=1+o(1).
\]

---

### 3.  Proportion of \(t\) for which \(a\) is a fourth power (\(p\equiv1\pmod4\))

Let \(\psi\) be a primitive quartic character (\(\psi^{2}=\chi\)).
The indicator of a fourth power is  

\[
\mathbf 1_{\text{4th}}(a)=\frac{1+\psi(a)+\psi^{2}(a)+\psi^{3}(a)}{4}.
\]

Summing over \(t\) we obtain

\[
\frac{1}{p}\sum_{t}\mathbf 1_{\text{4th}}(t^{2}+5)
    =\frac14+\frac{1}{4p}\Bigl(\sum\psi(t^{2}+5)+\sum\psi^{3}(t^{2}+5)\Bigr)
      +\frac{1}{4p}\sum\chi(t^{2}+5).
\]

The last sum is \(-1/(4p)\). The two sums involving \(\psi\) are
character sums of a non‑trivial character over a quadratic polynomial;
by Weil’s bound each is \(O(p^{1/2})\). Hence they vanish after division by
\(p\). Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{p}\#\{t\mid t^{2}+5\text{ is a fourth power}\}
      =\frac14+o(1).
\]

Consequently for \(p\equiv1\pmod4\)

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(t)
   =4\cdot\frac14+o(1)=1+o(1).
\]

---

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_p)}
        \sum_{y\in V(\mathbf F_p)}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1.
\]

Finally  

\[
\left\lfloor 100L\right\rfloor=\left\lfloor 100\right\rfloor = 100 .
\]

\[

### 1.  Where is \(\pi\) étale?

For a point \(y\) corresponding to \(t=t_{0}\) in a field \(k\) the fibre is  

\[
X_{y}= \operatorname{Spec}\bigl(k[x]/(x^{4}-(t_{0}^{2}+5))\bigr).
\]

The morphism is finite of degree \(4\) (the polynomial is monic in \(x\)).
It is étale exactly where the derivative with respect to \(x\) does not vanish:

\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\bigl(x^{4}-(t_{0}^{2}+5)\bigr)=4x^{3}.
\]

Hence étaleness fails precisely when  

* the characteristic is \(p=2\) (because \(4=0\) in \(\mathbf F_{2}\)), or  
* \(x=0\) lies in the fibre, i.e. when the constant term is zero:
  \(t_{0}^{2}+5=0\).

Thus for odd primes \(p\),

\[
V(\mathbf F_{p})=\Bigl\{\,t\in\mathbf F_{p}\;:\;t^{2}+5\neq 0\Bigr\},
\]

and for \(p=2\) the open \(V\) is empty.  For all \(p\ge 3\) the set
\(V(\mathbf F_{p})\) is non‑empty and dense in \(Y\).

Take any \(y\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\); then \(a:=t^{2}+5\) is a non‑zero element of

equation \(x^{4}=a\) has **exactly four distinct solutions** because the
characteristic does not divide \(4\) and \(a\neq 0\).

Consequently, for every \(y\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\)

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(y)=4 .
\]

---

Because the number of points in each fibre is the constant \(4\),

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)
      =\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\bigl(4\cdot\#V(\mathbf F_{p})\bigr)=4
\]

for every odd prime \(p\).  The limit as \(p\to\infty\) therefore exists and is

\[
L = 4 .
\]

\pi : X=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb Z[t,x]/(x^{4}-(t^{2}+5))\bigr)\longrightarrow

---

### 1.  Étale locus  

For a monic polynomial \(f(x)=x^{4}-a\) the discriminant is  

\[
\operatorname{Disc}(f)=256\,a^{3}.
\]

Here \(a=t^{2}+5\); therefore  

\[
\operatorname{Disc}(x^{4}-(t^{2}+5)) = 256\,(t^{2}+5)^{3}.
\]

The morphism \(\pi\) is étale exactly where this discriminant is invertible,
i.e. where  

* \(2\) is invertible (so we must be away from the prime \(p=2\)), and  
* \(t^{2}+5\neq 0\) in the residue field.

Hence the dense open subscheme \(V\subset Y\) is  

\[
V = Y\setminus\{\,p=2\}\setminus\{\,t\mid t^{2}+5=0\ \text{in the fibre}\,\}.
\]

For a prime \(p\neq 2\) the \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points of \(V\) are  

\[
V(\mathbb F_{p}) = \mathbb A^{1}(\mathbb F_{p})\setminus\{\,t\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid t^{2}=-5\}.
\]

The number of excluded points is \(0,1\) or \(2\) depending on whether \(-5\) is
a non‑square, a double root, or a square modulo \(p\).  
In any case, for large \(p\),

\[
\#V(\mathbb F_{p}) = p + O(1).
\]

---

### 2.  Size of a geometric fibre over \(V\)

Take a point \(y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) corresponding to \(t=a\in\mathbb F_{p}\) with
\(a^{2}+5\neq 0\).  
The fibre is  

\[
X_{y}= \operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb F_{p}[x]/(x^{4}-(a^{2}+5))\bigr).
\]

Because the discriminant is non‑zero, the polynomial \(x^{4}-(a^{2}+5)\) is
separable; thus \(X_{y}\) is a finite **étale** \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-scheme of degree
\(4\).  Consequently its geometric fibre consists of exactly \(4\) points,
independent of the field of definition of those points. Hence  

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(y)=4\qquad\text{for every }y\in V(\mathbb F_{p}).
\]

---

### 3.  Averaging over \(V(\mathbb F_{p})\)

Therefore  

\[
\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=4\;\#V(\mathbb F_{p}),
\]

and the average is  

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=4.
\]

This holds for every prime \(p\neq 2\); the primes that are omitted have
zero density, so the limit as \(p\to\infty\) exists and equals \(4\).

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=4.
\]

---

### 4.  Required integer

\[
\left\lfloor 100L\right\rfloor = \left\lfloor 100\cdot 4\right\rfloor = 400.
\]

\[
\boxed{400}
\]

The fibre of \(\pi\) over a point \(y\) with coordinate \(t=a\) is  

\[
\pi^{-1}(a)=\{x\in\mathbb F_p \mid x^{4}=a^{2}+5\}.
\]

Hence \(\#\pi^{-1}(a)\) is the number of fourth‑roots of the element  
\(s=a^{2}+5\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Where is \(\pi\) étale?

The map is étale at a point of the fibre iff the polynomial
\(x^{4}-(a^{2}+5)\) is separable, i.e. its derivative \(4x^{3}\) does not
vanish at any root.  
For \(p\neq 2\) this fails exactly when a root is \(x=0\), i.e. when
\(a^{2}+5=0\).  
In characteristic \(2\) the derivative is identically zero, so the map
is never étale.

Thus  

\[
V = Y\setminus\Bigl\{\,p=2\;\text{or}\;t^{2}+5=0\,\Bigr\}.
\]

For an odd prime \(p\),

\[
V(\mathbb F_{p})=\Bigl\{a\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid a^{2}\neq -5\Bigr\},
\qquad 
\#V(\mathbb F_{p}) = p-\bigl(1+\!\left(\frac{-5}{p}\right)\bigr),
\]

where \(\left(\frac{-5}{p}\right)\) is the Legendre symbol (the term
\(1\) appears because when \(-5\equiv 0\pmod p\) there is exactly one
solution \(a=0\)).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Number of points in a fibre

Let \(s=a^{2}+5\neq0\).  
In \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) the map \(x\mapsto x^{4}\) has kernel of
size  

\[
d=\gcd(4,p-1)=
\begin{cases}
4,& p\equiv1\pmod 4,\\[2pt]
2,& p\equiv3\pmod 4 .
\end{cases}
\]

Consequently  

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(a)=
\begin{cases}
4 &\text{if }p\equiv1\pmod4\text{ and }s\text{ is a fourth power},\\
2 &\text{if }p\equiv3\pmod4\text{ and }s\text{ is a square},\\
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Averaging over \(V(\mathbb F_{p})\)

Write \(\chi\) for the quadratic character modulo \(p\).
For \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) the condition “\(s\) is a square’’ is \(\chi(s)=1\);
for \(p\equiv1\pmod4\) let \(\psi\) be a quartic character (\(\psi^{2}=\chi\));
the condition “\(s\) is a fourth power’’ is \(\psi(s)=1\).

Using orthogonality of characters,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{p}\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{p}}\! \frac{1+\chi(s)}{2}
&= \frac12 + O\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt p}\right),\\[4pt]
\frac{1}{p}\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{p}}\! \frac{1+\psi(s)+\psi(s)^{2}+\psi(s)^{3}}{4}
&= \frac14 + O\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt p}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the proportion of \(a\) for which the fibre is non‑empty is
\(1/2\) when \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) and \(1/4\) when \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), up to an
error \(O(p^{-1/2})\).

Hence

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(a)
=
\begin{cases}
2\cdot\frac12 + O(p^{-1/2}) = 1+O(p^{-1/2}), & p\equiv3\pmod4,\\[4pt]
4\cdot\frac14 + O(p^{-1/2}) = 1+O(p^{-1/2}), & p\equiv1\pmod4 .
\end{cases}
\]

The error tends to zero as \(p\to\infty\). Therefore the limit exists and

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}
\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Required integer

\[
\left\lfloor 100L \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor 100\cdot 1 \right\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The limit \(L\) equals the average number of points in a fibre of \(\pi\) over the open set where \(\pi\) is finite étale.  

For a prime \(p\neq 2\) the morphism is étale away from the points where  
\(t^{2}+5\equiv 0\pmod p\).  
On the remaining \(p-O(1)\) points the fibre over \(y\) consists of the solutions of  

\[
x^{4}=y^{2}+5\qquad (\text{in }\mathbb{F}_{p}).
\]

If \(p\equiv 3\pmod 4\) the equation has either \(0\) or \(2\) solutions; it has \(2\) solutions exactly when \(y^{2}+5\) is a square, which happens for half of the \(y\)’s, giving an average fibre size \(\approx 2\cdot\frac12 =1\).

If \(p\equiv 1\pmod 4\) the equation has either \(0\) or \(4\) solutions; it has \(4\) solutions exactly when \(y^{2}+5\) is a fourth power, which occurs for a quarter of the \(y\)’s, again giving an average fibre size \(\approx 4\cdot\frac14 =1\).

The exceptional points where \(y^{2}+5=0\) contribute only \(O(1)\) terms, negligible in the limit. Hence  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1.
\]

Therefore  

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 100\cdot 1\big\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The morphism  

\[
\pi : X\longrightarrow Y ,\qquad 
X=\operatorname{Spec}\frac{\mathbb Z[t,x]}{(x^{4}-(t^{2}+5))},
\; Y=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t]
\]

is finite of degree \(4\).
It is étale at a point \(y\) of \(Y\) (i.e. at a prime \((p,t-a)\) with \(p\) a prime
and \(a\in\mathbb F_{p}\)) iff the polynomial  

\[
f_{a}(x)=x^{4}-(a^{2}+5)\in \mathbb F_{p}[x]
\]

is separable.  
The derivative is \(4x^{3}\); in characteristic \(\neq 2\) the only possible multiple
root is \(x=0\). Hence \(f_{a}\) is inseparable exactly when  

\[
a^{2}+5\equiv 0\pmod p .
\]

In characteristic \(2\) the derivative is zero, so the whole fibre over \(p=2\) is
non‑étale.  
Consequently  

\[
V = Y\setminus \bigl\{p=2\bigr\}\setminus\bigl\{t^{2}+5=0\}.
\]

For an odd prime \(p\) we have  

\[
V(\mathbb F_{p})=\{ a\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid a^{2}+5\neq 0\},
\qquad 
\#V(\mathbb F_{p}) = p-N_{p},
\]

where \(N_{p}= \#\{a\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid a^{2}=-5\}\in\{0,1,2\}\).

---

### Size of a fibre

For \(a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(a)\) is

\[
\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbb F_{p}[x]/(x^{4}-(a^{2}+5))\bigr),
\]

so its \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points are the solutions of  

\[
x^{4}=c,\qquad c:=a^{2}+5\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}.
\]

Let \(\chi_{2}\) be the quadratic character of \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) and,
when \(4\mid(p-1)\), let \(\chi_{4}\) be a character of order \(4\).
A standard formula gives the number of solutions of \(x^{4}=c\):

\[
\#\{x\mid x^{4}=c\}= \sum_{\substack{\chi^{4}=1}} \chi(c)
               = 1+\chi_{2}(c)+\mathbf 1_{4\mid(p-1)}\bigl(\chi_{4}(c)+\chi_{4}^{3}(c)\bigr).
\tag{1}
\]

Thus for \(a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\)

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(a)=1+\chi_{2}(a^{2}+5)+\mathbf 1_{4\mid(p-1)}\bigl(\chi_{4}(a^{2}+5)+\chi_{4}^{3}(a^{2}+5)\bigr).
\]

---

### Averaging over \(V(\mathbb F_{p})\)

Define  

\[
S_{p}= \sum_{a\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(a).
\]

Using the expression above,

\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{p}
&= (p-N_{p}) 
   +\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{p}}\chi_{2}(a^{2}+5)
   -\!\!\sum_{\substack{a^{2}+5=0}}\!\!\chi_{2}(0)\\
&\qquad+\mathbf 1_{4\mid(p-1)}\Bigl(
        \sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{p}}\chi_{4}(a^{2}+5)
       +\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{p}}\chi_{4}^{3}(a^{2}+5)\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

The sums of non‑trivial characters over a quadratic polynomial are classical
Weil sums; they satisfy  

\[
\Bigl|\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{p}}\chi(a^{2}+5)\Bigr|\le 2\sqrt{p},
\]

hence each of them is \(O(\sqrt{p})\).  
Therefore  

\[
S_{p}= (p-N_{p})+O(\sqrt{p}).
\]

Dividing by \(\#V(\mathbb F_{p})=p-N_{p}\) we obtain

\[
\frac{S_{p}}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}=1+O(p^{-1/2})\xrightarrow[p\to\infty]{}1 .
\]

Consequently  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}
      \sum_{y\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)=1 .
\]

---

### Final computation

\[
100L = 100\cdot 1 = 100,\qquad 
\bigl\lfloor 100L\bigr\rfloor = 100 .
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

Define  

\[
X=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb{Z}[1/7][t,w]\big/(w^{7}-t(t-1)(t-2))\Bigr)
\]

and let \(\pi:X\to Y\) be the morphism induced by the inclusion of rings.  
Let  

\[
V\subset Y
\]

be the open subscheme where the element \(t(t-1)(t-2)\) is invertible (i.e. the points with \(t\neq 0,1,2\)).  Over \(V\) the morphism \(\pi\) is finite étale of some degree \(d\).

For each prime \(p\neq 7\) write \(V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) for the set of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points of \(V\).  Define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x).
\]

Using the Chebotarev density theorem for the finite étale cover \(\pi|_{V}\), compute the value of \(L\).

Put your final answer inside \boxed{}.

\[

\]

The condition “\(a\) is a 7‑th power’’ is equivalent to the Frobenius element being the identity in \(G\).  
Hence the density of such points is \(1/|G| = 1/7\).

Consequently  

\[
L = 7 \times \frac{1}{7}=1.

The cover \(\pi|_{V}:X|_{V}\to V\) is defined by the equation  

\[
w^{7}=t(t-1)(t-2)=:a .

prime \(7\)).  Consequently \(\pi|_{V}\) is a finite étale morphism of
degree \(7\).

For a finite étale cover, the Chebotarev density theorem says that the
average number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points in a fibre equals the
average number of fixed points of a random element of the monodromy
group acting on a geometric fibre.  The monodromy group acts **transitively**
on the \(7\) geometric points of a fibre (the cover is connected), so by
Burnside’s lemma the average number of fixed points of a random group
element is exactly the number of orbits, i.e. \(1\).

the fibre consists of the solutions of \(w^{7}=a\) in \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\).
If \(p\equiv 1\pmod 7\) a proportion \(1/7\) of the non‑zero elements are
\(7\)th powers, giving \(7\) solutions for those \(t\) and none for the
others; the average is \(7\cdot\frac{1}{7}=1\).  If \(p\not\equiv 1\pmod 7\)

every fibre has exactly one \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-point.  In all cases the
average over \(V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) is \(1\).

Hence

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=1 .
\]

\[
\boxed{1}

\[
X=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb{Z}[t,u,x]\big/(x^{5}-(t+u))\Bigr)
\]

\(\mathbb{Z}[t,u]\hookrightarrow \mathbb{Z}[t,u,x]/(x^{5}-(t+u))\).

Let  

\[
V = Y\setminus V(t+u)=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb{Z}[t,u,(t+u)^{-1}]\Bigr)
\]

be the open subscheme where the element \(t+u\) is invertible.  
The restriction \(\pi|_{V}: X_V:=\pi^{-1}(V)\to V\) is finite étale.

For each prime \(p\) denote by \(V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) the set of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points of \(V\).  
Define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{y\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(y)(\mathbb{F}_{p}),
\]

the limit of the average number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points in the fibres of \(\pi|_{V}\) as \(p\) tends to infinity.

Using the Chebotarev density theorem for finite étale covers over function fields, compute \(\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor\).

w^{11}=f(a),\qquad f(t)=t^{5}+t+1 .
\]

---

### 1.  Discriminant and the open set \(V\)

For a polynomial \(X^{11}-c\) the discriminant is  

\[
\Delta = (-1)^{55}\,11^{11}\,c^{10}.
\]

Hence  

\[
\Delta(t)=\pm 11^{11}\bigl(t^{5}+t+1\bigr)^{10}.
\]

Thus  

\[
V=Y\setminus V(\Delta)=\{\,p\neq 11\text{ and }t\in\mathbb{F}_{p}\mid f(t)\neq 0\,\}.
\]

On \(V\) the map \(\pi\) is finite étale; in particular the fibre
contains only solutions of the equation \(w^{11}=f(t)\) with \(f(t)\neq0\).

---

### 2.  Number of solutions of \(w^{11}=c\) in \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)

Let \(c\neq0\).  
Write \(d=\gcd(11,p-1)\).  
The multiplicative group \(\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\times}\) is cyclic of order \(p-1\);
the map \(x\mapsto x^{11}\) has image of size \((p-1)/d\) and each element
in the image has exactly \(d\) pre‑images.  

Consequently  

* if \(c\) is an \(11\)‑th power in \(\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\times}\) then the equation
  has exactly \(d\) solutions,
* otherwise it has no solution.

Thus for a **non‑zero** \(c\),

\[
\#\{w\mid w^{11}=c\}= 
\begin{cases}
d &\text{if }c\in (\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\times})^{11},\\[2pt]
0 &\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

The probability that a random non‑zero element of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\) is an
\(11\)-th power equals \(1/d\). Hence the **expected** number of solutions for a
random non‑zero \(c\) is

\[
\frac{1}{d}\cdot d = 1 .
\]

---

### 3.  Averaging over the fibres of \(\pi\)

For \(t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) we have \(c=f(t)\neq0\).  
Let \(\chi\) be a primitive character of order \(d\) of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\times}\).
The indicator that \(c\) is an \(11\)‑th power can be written

\[
\mathbf{1}_{c\in (\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\times})^{11}}
   =\frac{1}{d}\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}\chi^{\,j}(c).
\]

Therefore

\[
\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)
   =\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}
      d\;\mathbf{1}_{f(t)\in (\mathbb{F}_{p}^{\times})^{11}}
   =\frac{1}{d}\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}
      d\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\chi^{\,j}\!\bigl(f(t)\bigr).
\]

The term \(j=0\) contributes \(|V(\mathbb{F}_{p})|\).
For each non‑trivial \(j\) the inner sum is a character sum over a
degree‑5 polynomial; by the Weil bound it is \(O(\sqrt{p})\).
Hence

\[
\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)
   =|V(\mathbb{F}_{p})|+O(\sqrt{p}).
\]

Dividing by \(|V(\mathbb{F}_{p})|\) and letting \(p\to\infty\) gives

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{|V(\mathbb{F}_{p})|}
      \sum_{t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)=1 .
\]

(The finitely many points where \(f(t)=0\) are omitted from \(V\); they are
\(O(1)\) in number and do not affect the limit.)

**3.  Number of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points in a fibre**

Let \(g=\gcd(11,p-1)\).  
In the multiplicative group \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\!*}\) the map \(x\mapsto x^{11}\) has

* kernel of size \(g\),
* image of size \((p-1)/g\).

Hence for a non‑zero element \(a\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\!*}\)

\[
\#\{\,w\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid w^{11}=a\,\}
=\begin{cases}
g &\text{if }a\in (\mathbb F_{p}^{\!*})^{11},\\[2mm]
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

If \(a=0\) the only solution is \(w=0\).

Because we are on \(V\) we always have \(f(t)\neq0\); therefore for each
\(t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\)

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)=
\begin{cases}
g &\text{if }f(t)\text{ is an }11\text{‑th power in }\mathbb F_{p}^{\!*},\\[2mm]
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**4.  How often is \(f(t)\) an 11‑th power?**

Let  

\[
S_{p}= \{\,t\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid f(t)\neq0,\;f(t)\in (\mathbb F_{p}^{\!*})^{11}\,\}.
\]

The set of 11‑th powers in \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\!*}\) has cardinality \((p-1)/g\).
For a polynomial of fixed degree (here \(\deg f=5\)) the values
\(f(t)\) are “almost uniformly” distributed:
each value \(a\) occurs at most \(5\) times, so

\[
\#\{\,t\mid f(t)=a\,\}=1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{p}\right)
\qquad (p\to\infty).
\]

Consequently  

\[
\#S_{p}= \frac{p-1}{g}+O(1).
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------

**5.  The average number of points in a fibre**

Denote by \(N_{p}\) the number of roots of \(f\) in \(\mathbb F_{p}\);  
\(N_{p}\le 5\).  Then \(|V(\mathbb F_{p})|=p-N_{p}\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{|V(\mathbb F_{p})|}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)
&=\frac{1}{p-N_{p}}\; g\;\#S_{p}\\[2mm]
&=\frac{1}{p-N_{p}}\; g\left(\frac{p-1}{g}+O(1)\right)\\[2mm]
&= \frac{p-1+O(g)}{p-N_{p}}
=1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{p}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the quantity tends to \(1\) as \(p\to\infty\).

For a prime \(p\neq 11\) and a point \(y\) corresponding to \(t\in\mathbb F_{p}\) with
\(f(t)=t^{5}+t+1\neq 0\), the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(y)\) consists of the solutions of  

\[
w^{11}=f(t)\qquad\text{in }\mathbb F_{p}.
\]

Let  

\[
g(p)=\gcd(11,p-1).
\]

The map \(w\mapsto w^{11}\) on \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) has kernel of size \(g(p)\) and
image of size \((p-1)/g(p)\).  
Thus for a non‑zero \(a\in\mathbb F_{p}\),

\[
\#\{w\in\mathbb F_{p}\mid w^{11}=a\}= 
\begin{cases}
g(p) &\text{if } a\in (\mathbb F_{p}^{\times})^{11},\\[2pt]
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Consequently, for \(t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\),

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)=g(p)\,\mathbf 1_{\{f(t)\in (\mathbb F_{p}^{\times})^{11}\}} .
\]

The set of 11‑th powers in \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) has proportion \(1/g(p)\); for a
random non‑zero value of the polynomial \(f(t)\) this proportion is the same up
to an error \(O(p^{-1/2})\) (Weil bound for the image of a degree‑5 polynomial).
Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)
= g(p)\cdot\frac{1}{g(p)}+o(1)=1+o(1).
\]

Taking the limit as \(p\to\infty\) we obtain  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(t)=1.
\]

Finally  

\[
\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor = \bigl\lfloor 100 \times 1 \bigr\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

problems.problem:
Let  

\[
Y \;=\; \operatorname{Spec}\!\Bigl(\mathbb{Z}\!\bigl[\tfrac{1}{5},\,t,\,(t^{2}+3)^{-1}\bigr]\Bigr)
\]

and define  

\[
X \;=\; \operatorname{Spec}\!\Bigl(\mathbb{Z}\!\bigl[\tfrac{1}{5},\,t,\,(t^{2}+3)^{-1},\,x\bigr]\big/\bigl(x^{5}-(t^{2}+3)\bigr)\Bigr).
\]

Let \(\pi : X \to Y\) be the morphism induced by the inclusion of rings.
For a prime \(p\neq 5\) let  

\[
V(\mathbb{F}_{p}) \;=\; \bigl\{\, t\in\mathbb{F}_{p}\mid t^{2}+3\neq 0 \,\bigr\},
\]

the set of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points of \(Y\).  
For each \(t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(t)\) is the zero‑scheme of the
polynomial \(x^{5}=t^{2}+3\) in \(\mathbb{A}^{1}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\).

Define  

\[
L \;=\; \lim_{p\to\infty}\;\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\,\sum_{t\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbb{F}_{p}),
\]

the limit of the average number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points in the fibres of \(\pi\) as \(p\) grows.
Using the Chebotarev density theorem for the finite étale cover \(\pi\), compute  

\[
\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor .
\]

Put your final answer inside \boxed{}.
all_solutions:
The morphism  

\[
\pi : X \longrightarrow Y ,\qquad 
X=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb{Z}[1/5,t,(t^{2}+3)^{-1},x]/(x^{5}-(t^{2}+3))\Bigr)
\]

is finite étale of degree \(5\): we have inverted \(5\) and the discriminant
\(t^{2}+3\), so the polynomial \(x^{5}-(t^{2}+3)\) is separable and defines a
finite étale cover of the affine line minus the two points where
\(t^{2}+3=0\).

For a prime \(p\neq 5\) and \(t\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) the fibre is  

\[
\pi^{-1}(t)=\{x\in\mathbf{A}^{1}_{\mathbf{F}_{p}}\mid x^{5}=t^{2}+3\}.
\]

Thus  

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf{F}_{p})=\#\{x\in\mathbf{F}_{p}\mid x^{5}=a\},
\qquad a=t^{2}+3\neq 0 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Chebotarev interpretation

Let \(K=\mathbf{Q}(t)\) be the function field of \(Y\) and let  

\[
L=K\bigl(\root 5\of{t^{2}+3}\bigr)
\]

be the function field of \(X\).  
The extension \(L/K\) has degree \(5\) and is separable.  
Let \(\widetilde L\) be its Galois closure and \(G=\operatorname{Gal}(\widetilde L/K)\).
The set \(S\) of geometric points of the generic fibre of \(\pi\) consists of the
\(5\) distinct roots of \(x^{5}=t^{2}+3\); \(G\) acts on \(S\) by permutation.
Because the polynomial is irreducible over \(K\), the action of \(G\) on \(S\) is
**transitive**.

For a prime \(p\not=5\) and a point \(t\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) the Frobenius
conjugacy class \(\operatorname{Frob}_{p,t}\subset G\) describes the permutation
of the five roots induced by the map \(x\mapsto x^{p}\).  
The number of \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-points in the fibre equals the number of fixed
points of this permutation:

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf{F}_{p})=\#\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{Frob}_{p,t}\,|\,S).
\]

Hence  

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf{F}_{p})
=\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}
\#\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{Frob}_{p,t}\,|\,S).
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Averaging over Frobenius elements

Chebotarev’s density theorem tells us that, when \(p\) varies, the Frobenius
conjugacy classes become equidistributed in \(G\).  
Therefore the limit

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf{F}_{p})
\]

equals the **average number of fixed points of a random element of \(G\) acting
on the set \(S\)**.

By Burnside’s lemma, the average number of fixed points of a group action is
exactly the number of orbits of the action.  
Since the action of \(G\) on the five roots is transitive, there is **one**
orbit. Consequently

\[
L = 1 .
\]

(The omission of the at most two points where \(t^{2}+3=0\) does not affect the
limit, because \(\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p}) = p+O(1)\).)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Computing \(\lfloor 100L\rfloor\)

\[
L = 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 100L = 100,\qquad
\bigl\lfloor 100L \bigr\rfloor = 100 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
\[
\boxed{100}

The morphism  

\[
\pi : X\longrightarrow Y,
\qquad 
X=\operatorname{Spec}\Bigl(\mathbb Z[1/5,t,(t^{2}+3)^{-1},x]/(x^{5}-(t^{2}+3))\Bigr)
\]

is finite étale of degree \(5\) (the equation \(x^{5}=t^{2}+3\) is separable because we have removed the points where \(t^{2}+3=0\) and we work away from the prime \(5\)).  
For a prime \(p\neq5\) and a point \(t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) the fibre is

\[
\pi^{-1}(t)=\{x\in\mathbb A^{1}_{\mathbb F_{p}} \mid x^{5}=t^{2}+3\}.
\]

Hence the number of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points in the fibre equals the number of solutions of the equation
\(x^{5}=a\) with \(a=t^{2}+3\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\).

---

### Counting solutions of \(x^{5}=a\) in \(\mathbb F_{p}\)

*If \(5\nmid (p-1)\):* the map \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) is a bijection of \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\); therefore for every \(a\neq0\) there is exactly one solution, i.e. \(\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbb F_{p})=1\).

*If \(5\mid (p-1)\):* the multiplicative group \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) is cyclic of order \(p-1\).  
The kernel of \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) has size \(5\); the image consists of the subgroup \((\mathbb F_{p}^{\times})^{5}\) of index \(5\).  
Thus

\[
\#\{x\mid x^{5}=a\}= \begin{cases}
5 & \text{if } a\in (\mathbb F_{p}^{\times})^{5},\\[2pt]
0 & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

The proportion of elements of \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) that are 5‑th powers is \(1/5\). Consequently the average number of solutions is  

\[
5\cdot\frac15 = 1 .
\]

---

### Averaging over the base points

The map \(t\mapsto a=t^{2}+3\) is a 2‑to‑1 map onto its image, and the image is a set of size \(\frac{p-1}{2}+O(1)\).  
Thus the values \(a\) are equidistributed in \(\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\) as \(p\to\infty\).  
Hence the average of \(\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbb F_{p})\) over all \(t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) equals the average of the numbers of solutions of \(x^{5}=a\) over a uniformly random \(a\in\mathbb F_{p}^{\times}\), which we have just computed to be \(1\).

Therefore  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}
          \sum_{t\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbb F_{p}) = 1 .
\]

(Equivalently, Chebotarev’s density theorem tells us that for a degree‑\(5\) étale cover the average number of fixed points of Frobenius—hence the average fibre size—is \(1\).)

Finally,

\[
\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor = \bigl\lfloor 100\cdot 1 \bigr\rfloor = 100 .
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The fibre over a point \(t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) is the set of solutions of  

\[
x^{5}=t^{2}+3\; (=a)\qquad\text{in }\mathbf F_{p}.
\]

Let \(d=\gcd (5,p-1)\).  
The map \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) on \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\) is a homomorphism whose kernel has
size \(d\); hence  

* if \(a\) lies in the image \((\mathbf F_{p}^{\times})^{5}\) the equation has exactly \(d\) solutions,
* otherwise it has no solution.

Thus  

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})=
\begin{cases}
d &\text{if }t^{2}+3\in (\mathbf F_{p}^{\times})^{5},\\[2pt]
0 &\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

Consequently  

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})
   = d\;
     \Pr_{t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\bigl(t^{2}+3\in (\mathbf F_{p}^{\times})^{5}\bigr).
\]

---

### 1.  When \(5\nmid(p-1)\)

Then \(d=1\) and the map \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) is a bijection, so every non‑zero \(a\) is a
fifth power. Hence the probability above equals \(1\) and the average equals \(1\).

---

### 2.  When \(5\mid(p-1)\)

Now \(d=5\). Exactly one fifth of the elements of \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\) are fifth powers.
The values \(a=t^{2}+3\) (with \(a\neq0\)) run over the set  

\[
S=\{a\in\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\mid a-3 \text{ is a quadratic residue}\}.
\]

Using the quadratic character \(\chi\) and a primitive character \(\psi\) of order \(5\),

\[
\mathbf 1_{(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times})^{5}}(a)=\frac{1}{5}\sum_{k=0}^{4}\psi^{k}(a),
\]

so

\[
\Pr_{t\in V}\bigl(t^{2}+3\in (\mathbf F_{p}^{\times})^{5}\bigr)
 =\frac{1}{\#V}\sum_{t\in V}\frac{1}{5}\sum_{k=0}^{4}\psi^{k}(t^{2}+3)
 =\frac{1}{5}+O(p^{-1/2}).
\]

(The error term follows from the Weil bound for character sums.)  
Therefore  

\[
\text{average}= d\left(\frac{1}{5}+O(p^{-1/2})\right)=5\cdot\frac{1}{5}+O(p^{-1/2})=1+O(p^{-1/2}).
\]

---

### 3.  Limit

In both cases the average equals \(1+O(p^{-1/2})\).  Hence

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}
   \sum_{t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})=1.
\]

Finally  

\[
\Bigl\lfloor 100\,L\Bigr\rfloor =\bigl\lfloor 100\cdot 1\bigr\rfloor =100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The fibre over a point \(t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) is the set of solutions of  

\[
x^{5}=t^{2}+3 \qquad (\;t^{2}+3\neq 0\; )
\]

in \(\mathbf F_{p}\).

---

### 1.  Number of solutions of \(x^{5}=a\) in \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\)

Let \(d=\gcd(5,p-1)\).

* The map \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) on \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\) is a homomorphism with kernel of size \(d\) and image of size \((p-1)/d\).
* For a given \(a\neq 0\) the equation has a solution iff \(a\) lies in the image; when it does, there are exactly \(d\) solutions.

Hence for each \(t\),

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})=
\begin{cases}
d &\text{if }t^{2}+3\in (\mathbf F_{p}^{\times})^{5},\\[2mm]
0 &\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

---

### 2.  Probability that \(t^{2}+3\) is a 5‑th power

* If \(p\equiv 1\pmod 5\) then \(d=5\).  
  The image of the 5‑th‑power map has size \((p-1)/5\); therefore a random non‑zero element is a 5‑th power with probability \(\frac{1}{5}\).

* If \(p\not\equiv 1\pmod 5\) then \(d=1\) (the map \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) is a bijection), so **every** non‑zero element is a 5‑th power.  

In both cases the expected number of points in the fibre is  

\[
\mathbb E\bigl[\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})\bigr]
= d\;\Pr\bigl(t^{2}+3\text{ is a 5‑th power}\bigr)=1 .
\]

The two values of \(t\) for which \(t^{2}+3=0\) are omitted from \(V(\mathbf F_{p})\); they affect the average by at most \(O(1/p)\), which disappears in the limit.

Thus for every prime \(p\neq5\),

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p}) = 1 + O\!\left(\frac{1}{p}\right).
\]

---

### 3.  Limit \(L\)

Taking \(p\to\infty\),

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p}) = 1 .
\]

(Equivalently, Chebotarev applied to the degree‑5 Kummer cover gives the same result: the monodromy group is the affine group \(\operatorname{AGL}(1,5)\) of order \(20\); the average number of fixed points of a random element of a transitive group is \(1\) by Burnside’s lemma.)

---

### 4.  Required integer

\[
\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor = \bigl\lfloor 100\cdot 1 \bigr\rfloor = 100 .
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The fibre over a point \(t\in V(\mathbf{F}_p)\) consists of the solutions of  

\[
x^{5}=t^{2}+3\qquad(\ast )
\]

in \(\mathbf{F}_p\).  
Let  

\[
N(t)=\#\{x\in\mathbf{F}_p\mid x^{5}=t^{2}+3\}.
\]

The required average is  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_p)}\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf{F}_p)} N(t).
\]

---

### 1.  Re‑express the sum

\[
\sum_{t\in V(\mathbf{F}_p)} N(t)=
\sum_{t\in V}\;\sum_{x\in\mathbf{F}_p}\mathbf 1_{x^{5}=t^{2}+3}
=
\sum_{x\in\mathbf{F}_p^{\!*}}\;\#\{t\in\mathbf{F}_p\mid t^{2}=x^{5}-3\}.
\]

(The term \(x=0\) gives no admissible \(t\) because then \(t^{2}+3=0\), which is excluded from \(V\).)

For a fixed \(x\neq0\) the equation \(t^{2}=x^{5}-3\) has  

\[
1+\Bigl(\frac{x^{5}-3}{p}\Bigr)
\]

solutions, where \(\bigl(\frac{\cdot}{p}\bigr)\) is the Legendre symbol (with the convention \(\bigl(\frac{0}{p}\bigr)=0\)). Hence  

\[
\sum_{t\in V} N(t)=\sum_{x\in\mathbf{F}_p^{\!*}}\Bigl[1+\Bigl(\frac{x^{5}-3}{p}\Bigr)\Bigr]
=(p-1)+S(p),
\]

where  

\[
S(p)=\sum_{x\in\mathbf{F}_p^{\!*}}\Bigl(\frac{x^{5}-3}{p}\Bigr).
\]

---

### 2.  Size of \(V(\mathbf{F}_p)\)

\(V(\mathbf{F}_p)=\{t\mid t^{2}+3\neq0\}\).  
The equation \(t^{2}+3=0\) has \(1+\bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\bigr)\) solutions, so  

\[
\#V(\mathbf{F}_p)=p-\bigl[1+\bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\bigr)\bigr]=p-1-\bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\bigr).
\]

In particular \(\#V(\mathbf{F}_p)=p+O(1)\).

---

### 3.  Asymptotics of the character sum \(S(p)\)

The sum \(S(p)\) is a non‑trivial quadratic character sum over the polynomial
\(f(x)=x^{5}-3\) of degree \(5\). By the Weil bound (or Riemann–Hurwitz),

\[
|S(p)|\le (5-1)\sqrt{p}=4\sqrt{p}.
\]

Thus  

\[
\frac{S(p)}{p}\longrightarrow 0\qquad (p\to\infty).
\]

---

### 4.  Limit \(L\)

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_p)}\sum_{t\in V} N(t)
= \frac{(p-1)+S(p)}{p-1-\bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\bigr)}
= 1+\frac{S(p)}{p}+O\!\left(\frac{1}{p}\right).
\]

Taking the limit as \(p\to\infty\),

\[
L = 1.
\]

---

### 5.  Required integer

\[
\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor = \bigl\lfloor 100\cdot 1 \bigr\rfloor = 100.
\]

\[
\boxed{100}
\]

The fibre over a point \(t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) is defined by  

\[
x^{5}=t^{2}+3\quad (\neq 0).
\]

Hence we are counting the \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-solutions of the equation \(x^{5}=a\) with
\(a\in\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\).

In the multiplicative group \(\mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\) (cyclic of order \(p-1\)) the map  

\[
\phi : \mathbf F_{p}^{\times}\longrightarrow \mathbf F_{p}^{\times},\qquad \phi(x)=x^{5}
\]

has kernel of size \(\gcd(5,p-1)\) and image of size \((p-1)/\gcd(5,p-1)\).

* If \(p\equiv 1\pmod 5\) then \(\gcd(5,p-1)=5\).  
  The map \(\phi\) is \(5\)-to‑\(1\) and is surjective, so **every** \(a\neq 0\) has exactly \(5\) pre‑images.  
  Hence for all \(t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) we have \(\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})=5\).

* If \(p\equiv 2,3,4\pmod 5\) then \(\gcd(5,p-1)=1\).  
  The map \(\phi\) is a bijection, so each \(a\neq 0\) has exactly one pre‑image.  
  Thus \(\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf F_{p})=1\) for all \(t\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\).

Therefore the average number of points in a fibre for a fixed prime \(p\neq 5\) is

\[
A(p)=\begin{cases}
5 &\text{if } p\equiv 1\pmod 5,\\[2pt]
1 &\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

To obtain the limit \(L\) we use the Chebotarev (Dirichlet) density theorem: among the primes
\(p\neq 5\) the residue class \(1\bmod 5\) has natural density \(1/4\), while the other three
non‑zero residues each have density \(1/4\). Consequently

\[
L=\frac14\cdot5+\frac34\cdot1=\frac{5+3}{4}=2.
\]

Finally

\[
\big\lfloor 100L\big\rfloor =\big\lfloor 100\cdot 2\big\rfloor =\boxed{200}.
\]

For a prime \(p\neq 5\) let  

\[
Y(\mathbf F _p)=\{t\in\mathbf F _p\mid t^{2}+3\neq 0\},\qquad 
X_t=\pi^{-1}(t)=\{x\in\mathbf A^{1}_{\mathbf F _p}\mid x^{5}=t^{2}+3\}.

### 1.  Number of \(\mathbf F _p\)-points in a fibre  

Write \(a=t^{2}+3\in\mathbf F _p^{\times}\).
The equation \(x^{5}=a\) has a solution in \(\mathbf F _p\) iff \(a\) is a
\(5\)‑th power in the multiplicative group \(\mathbf F _p^{\times}\).
If a solution exists, the number of solutions equals  

\[
\gcd(5,p-1)=\begin{cases}
5 & p\equiv 1\pmod 5,\\[2mm]
1 & p\not\equiv 1\pmod 5 .
\end{cases}
\]

Thus for each \(t\)

\[
\#X_t(\mathbf F _p)=
\begin{cases}
5 &\text{if }p\equiv1\pmod5\text{ and }a\in(\mathbf F _p^{\times})^{5},\\[2mm]
1 &\text{if }p\not\equiv1\pmod5\ (\text{every }a\neq0\text{ is a }5\text{th power}),\\[2mm]
0 &\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

When \(p\not\equiv1\pmod5\) every non‑zero \(a\) is a \(5\)‑th power,
so every \(t\in Y(\mathbf F _p)\) contributes one point:
\[
\frac{1}{\#Y(\mathbf F _p)}\sum_{t\in Y(\mathbf F _p)}\#X_t(\mathbf F _p)=1 .

Consequently the set of \(t\) for which \(a\) is a \(5\)‑th power has size

\[
\frac{1}{5}\,\#Y(\mathbf F _p)+O(1),
\]

the error being bounded independently of \(p\).
Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{\#Y(\mathbf F _p)}\sum_{t\in Y(\mathbf F _p)}\#X_t(\mathbf F _p)
=5\cdot\frac{1}{5}+o(1)=1+o(1).
\]

### 3.  Limit \(L\)

Both congruence classes give the same limit, namely  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#Y(\mathbf F _p)}\sum_{t\in Y(\mathbf F _p)}
\#X_t(\mathbf F _p)=1 .
\]

(One can also obtain this from Chebotarev: the Galois closure of the
cover \(X\to Y\) has Galois group the Frobenius group of order \(20\);
the average number of fixed points of its elements is \(1\).)

Then \(\gcd(5,p-1)=1\); the map \(x\mapsto x^{5}\) is a bijection on \(\mathbf{F}_p^{\times}\).

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(t)(\mathbf{F}_p)=1 \qquad\forall\,t\in V(\mathbf{F}_p).
\]

### 2.  Primes \(p\equiv 1\pmod 5\)

Now \(d=5\). Let  

\[
H=(\mathbf{F}_p^{\times})^{5}\subset\mathbf{F}_p^{\times},
